physics: root-zone heating at about 38 °C takes low-grade heat; pipe-rail heating at 82 °C needs a heat pump
land: little yard left: a rooftop greenhouse or a neighbour's lot
demand: the heat offered could warm about 5,561–13,059 m² of greenhouse at 1.63–2.1 GJ/m² a year (Ontario, Manitoba measured); BC vegetable greenhouses use 1.3–2.0 GJ/m² a year of all energy (industry estimate, 2011). For scale: the City of Edmonton has 5 greenhouse farms, about 23,700 m², mostly potted plants; Division No. 11 about 108,000 m² (Census of Agriculture 2021)
time: greenhouses need most heat in winter nights, as data centres give it all year; and in BC from May to October 90% of greenhouse gas is burned for its CO₂, not its heat — about half the year's gas — so server heat replaces only part of it (BC Greenhouse Sector report, 2011)
money: Alberta greenhouses in 2023: investment $105–478 per m² by crop, natural gas $4–12 per m² a year (the heat a data centre could displace); about 85% heat with natural gas (Alberta Agriculture and Irrigation, 2023 survey of 53 growers). What a grower would pay for server heat is not published
